chapter_name: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to pinpoint the exact location of any object on a flat surface using a clever grid system created by René Descartes!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Imagine a city with streets running perfectly North-South and East-West. The Cartesian plane is similar. It uses two perpendicular number lines (x-axis and y-axis) intersecting at the 'Origin' (0,0) to map locations.
Every point has an address written as $(x, y)$. The first number ($x$) tells you how far to move left or right. The second number ($y$) tells you how far to move up or down.
The two axes divide the plane into four rooms called Quadrants. Quadrant I is $(+, +)$, Quadrant II is $(-, +)$, Quadrant III is $(-, -)$, and Quadrant IV is $(+, -)$.

fun_activity.title: 🚢 The Battleship Game
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a 10x10 Cartesian grid on a piece of paper. Hide 3 'ships' (dots) on different coordinates without showing your friend. Have your friend guess coordinates like (3, -2) to try and 'hit' your ships!

exam_tips: 📌 Always write the x-coordinate first! A common mistake is flipping $(3, 5)$ to mean 3 up and 5 right. It's always 3 right, 5 up.
📌 The coordinates of any point on the x-axis are $(x, 0)$ and on the y-axis are $(0, y)$.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Cartesian plane uses intersecting horizontal and vertical number lines to locate points.
⭐ A point is defined by an ordered pair $(x, y)$.
⭐ The plane is divided into four quadrants with distinct positive and negative sign patterns.
